moduleTitle: Extracting SMS messages using email service in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Describe what Testim's email service is.
Articulate when to use Testim's email service.
Explain the process of extracting SMS messages in a test using Testim's email service.

elements.description: Testim generates email addresses exclusively through its own built-in email service — there's no option to plug in a third-party email provider for this. Two address types are available: a permanent address, created once from Settings → Email Service → Generate Email Address; and a temporary address, generated fresh on every run via a Generate email address step in the test itself (shown as 'Temporary' in its title).

elements.term: Validate email and Extract Value together
elements.description: Validate email fetches the content of a Testim inbox (for a permanent or temporary address) as an array of all messages in that mailbox — confirming a message arrived. Extract Value then pulls just the specific, stable content needed out of that message (a code, a link) into a variable for later steps to use.

bulletPoints: Testim's email service is self-contained — addresses come only from Testim, not a third-party provider.
Permanent address: Settings → Email Service → Generate Email Address (one-time, reusable).
Temporary address: a Generate email address step in the test (fresh per run, labeled 'Temporary').
Validate email fetches inbox content; Extract Value pulls out the specific value needed.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: When to use Testim's email service

elements.description: The obvious case: any flow where the AUT itself sends an email — signup confirmation, password reset, order confirmation — and the test needs to receive and act on that email's content.

The less obvious, but exactly what this module is about: many applications and SMS/OTP providers can be configured to forward SMS content (like a one-time verification code) to an email address instead of, or in addition to, a phone number. When the AUT or its SMS provider is set up that way, Testim doesn't need any separate SMS API integration — the SMS content simply arrives as a message in a Testim email inbox, and it's read and extracted using the exact same Validate email / Extract Value mechanism as a normal email.

elements.text: This is the core idea behind the module's title: it's not that Testim has a dedicated SMS-reading feature — it's that routing SMS through email lets the email service double as the SMS-reading mechanism, avoiding the need for a separate SMS testing integration.

bulletPoints: Use Testim's email service directly whenever the AUT sends real emails that need to be validated or acted on.
Use it for SMS too, when the AUT/SMS provider can forward SMS content to an email address — same extraction mechanism, no separate SMS API needed.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Extracting an SMS-forwarded value from a test

elements.description: Rather than asserting on an entire forwarded-SMS message body, the recommended pattern is to extract only the specific, stable value needed — an OTP code, a verification link, a short confirmation phrase — and save it to a Testim variable so a later step (entering the code into the AUT, for example) can use it directly.

elements.term: Choosing permanent vs. temporary for this scenario
elements.description: A permanent address suits a recurring flow you test repeatedly (e.g. re-verifying the same test account's phone number). A temporary, freshly-generated address suits a scenario that needs a brand-new, never-before-used contact point on every run — such as testing that a new-user SMS-verification flow works for a genuinely new signup each time.

bulletPoints: Extract only the specific stable value (the OTP/code) from the forwarded SMS-as-email message — not the whole body.
Permanent address = recurring/reusable scenarios; temporary address = a fresh contact point needed every run.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming SMS testing requires a separate SMS/telephony API integration
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Reaching for a third-party SMS gateway API integration to read a verification code, when the AUT/provider can simply forward the SMS to an email address instead.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When SMS content can be routed to email, Testim's existing email service (Validate email + Extract Value) reads it — no separate SMS API integration needed.

examPitfalls.title: Asserting on an entire forwarded-SMS email body instead of extracting the needed value
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Writing a validation that checks the full forwarded message text matches exactly, which breaks the moment any unrelated part of the forwarding template changes.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Extract only the specific, stable value you actually need (the OTP code) into a variable, rather than validating the entire message body.

examPitfalls.title: Using a permanent address for a scenario that needs a brand-new contact point every run
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Reusing the same permanent Testim email address to repeatedly test a new-signup SMS-verification flow that specifically needs an unused contact point.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use a temporary, freshly generated address (via the Generate email address step) when the scenario needs a fresh, never-before-seen address on each run — reserve the permanent address for recurring, repeat-use flows.

options.text: A third-party email provider Testim connects to for generating test addresses.
Testim's own built-in mechanism for generating and reading email addresses/messages — permanent (via Settings) or temporary (via a test step).
A paid add-on unrelated to test steps.
A feature that only works with Gmail accounts.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's fully self-contained — no external provider involved.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Testim generates email addresses exclusively through its own built-in email service, with permanent addresses created via Settings → Email Service and temporary addresses generated per run via a Generate email address step — not a third-party provider, a Gmail-only feature, or something disconnected from test steps.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How is a permanent Testim email address created?

options.text: Settings → Email Service → Generate Email Address.
By adding a Generate email address step inside the test.
Permanent addresses aren't supported — every address is temporary.
By connecting an external email provider's API key.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a one-time setup action, not a per-run test step.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A permanent email address is created once, from Settings → Email Service → Generate Email Address. A Generate email address STEP inside a test instead produces a fresh, temporary address on every run — the two are distinct mechanisms.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why would a tester use Testim's email service to extract an SMS-based verification code, rather than integrating a separate SMS API?

options.text: Because Testim cannot handle SMS in any form.

Because when the AUT/SMS provider can forward SMS content to an email address, Testim's existing email service can read it using the same Validate email / Extract Value mechanism — no separate SMS integration needed.
Because SMS messages are always identical to emails technically.
Because Testim's email service physically sends SMS messages.

practiceQuiz.hint: The trick is routing SMS through email, not a special SMS feature.
practiceQuiz.rationale: When SMS content is routed to email, the SMS effectively becomes a message in a Testim inbox — readable and extractable with the same Validate email / Extract Value pattern used for any email, avoiding the need for a dedicated SMS API integration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A test needs to repeatedly verify a new signup's SMS-based phone verification, where each signup must use a brand-new, never-before-used contact point. Which type of Testim email address fits?

options.text: A permanent address, reused every run.
A temporary address, freshly generated on each run via a Generate email address step.
Either works identically for this scenario.
Neither — this scenario isn't supported by Testim's email service.

practiceQuiz.hint: The scenario explicitly needs a fresh, unused contact point each time.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A temporary address, generated fresh via a Generate email address step, gives a brand-new contact point on every run — exactly what a 'must be never-before-used' signup/verification scenario needs. A permanent address would reuse the same address every time, the opposite of what's required.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why is it recommended to extract only the OTP code from a forwarded SMS-as-email message rather than validating the entire message body?

options.text: Extracting values is not actually supported for forwarded messages.
Extracting only the stable value needed avoids breaking the test when unrelated parts of the forwarding/email template change.
Whole-message validation runs faster than value extraction.
It has no effect on test stability either way.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about maintainability when the message template changes.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Extracting only the specific, stable value needed (the OTP code) keeps the test focused on what actually matters, so it doesn't break every time an unrelated part of the forwarding/email template is redesigned.

quickRecap.value: Self-contained — no third-party provider; permanent (Settings) or temporary (test step) addresses.
Settings → Email Service → Generate Email Address — one-time, reusable.
Generate email address step — fresh per run, labeled 'Temporary'.
If SMS can be forwarded to an email address, Testim's email service reads it — no separate SMS API needed.
Pull only the specific stable value (OTP, link) into a variable, not the whole body.
